intervention_label: Atorvastatin (mevalonate-pathway / protein geranylgeranylation blockade) repurposed for uterine leiomyosarcoma
mechanism: Atorvastatin blocks HMG-CoA reductase and drains the isoprenoid pool downstream of mevalonate. In uLMS cells the consequence that matters is loss of geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate, so small GTPases such as Rap1A/Rap1B go unprenylated and the contractile smooth-muscle program collapses along with proliferation.
rationale: This is one of very few published ideas tested in uterine LMS cells and uterine LMS xenografts rather than borrowed from another sarcoma. Adding geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate back rescued the phenotype, which is the kind of on-mechanism control that usually separates a real dependency from generic statin cytotoxicity. Her tumour is hormone-receptor negative and systemic-therapy naive, so a cheap oral agent with an independent mechanism is worth a lab's time even though nobody would give it as therapy on this evidence. The reported effect was partial - roughly half of tumour growth - not tumour clearance.
novelty: No statin or mevalonate-pathway agent appears in this case's trials, clinical-evidence or preclinical-evidence files, and there is no registered oncology trial of a statin in leiomyosarcoma of any site.

key_manuscripts.finding: Atorvastatin arrested human uLMS cell lines in G0/G1 and cut the contractile phenotype, with geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate rescuing both effects and Rap1A/Rap1B unprenylation confirming the mechanism. Xenograft growth fell by about 50% without weight loss or serum ALT/creatinine changes.

developability: Atorvastatin is generic and orally available, so the gap is not chemistry but dose: the antitumour concentrations in these experiments sit well above what lipid-lowering dosing achieves in plasma. A repurposing trial would have to establish that an oncology dose is both reachable and tolerable.
risks: Exposure gap between lipid-lowering dosing and the concentrations that killed cells in vitro
Single laboratory, one publication, no independent replication yet
Statin myopathy and rhabdomyolysis risk would rise on cytotoxic chemotherapy
Xenograft response was partial growth inhibition, not regression
caveats: Published in mid-2026 and not yet replicated elsewhere. The cell lines used are the same handful (SK-LMS-1, SK-UT-1 lineage) that carry known drift from primary uLMS biology.

intervention_label: SUV39H2 inhibitor OTS186935 plus a PARP inhibitor
target_feature_label: High-grade uterine leiomyosarcoma histology; DNA-repair capacity still unmeasured
mechanism: SUV39H2 methylates H3K9 and also marks H2AX at K134, which is needed for efficient gamma-H2AX deposition and double-strand-break repair. Inhibiting it leaves breaks poorly signalled, and layering PARP inhibition on top removes the single-strand repair route that would otherwise convert those lesions back into something survivable.
rationale: SUV39H2 protein is higher in uLMS than in matched myometrium or leiomyoma, so the target is anchored in the right tissue rather than inferred from a pan-cancer average. The synthetic lethality with olaparib was shown in uLMS lines and then in uLMS xenografts. That matters here because her HRD status is unmeasured: a combination that manufactures a repair defect rather than requiring a pre-existing one would not be gated on the BRCA/HRD test she has not had. The comparison arm is olaparib alone, which is itself of limited single-agent value in unselected uLMS.
novelty: OTS186935 is an academic/tool-stage SUV39H2 inhibitor with no IND and no registered trial in any indication; no SUV39H2 agent appears anywhere upstream in this case.

key_manuscripts.finding: SUV39H2 was overexpressed in uLMS tissue relative to normal myometrium and leiomyoma, and OTS186935 reduced viability of SK-LMS-1 and SK-UT-1 with synthetic lethality when combined with olaparib. ChIP-seq and immunofluorescence tied the effect to disrupted gamma-H2AX deposition, and the combination held up in subcutaneous uLMS xenografts.

model_systems: uLMS vs myometrium vs leiomyoma IHC
developability: OTS186935 is a chemical probe from an academic programme with no clinical-grade successor. Someone would need to take the series through medicinal chemistry and IND-enabling work, or find a second SUV39H2 chemotype, before this could be tested in a patient.
risks: H3K9 methyltransferase inhibition has broad chromatin consequences and no clinical safety precedent
Both uLMS lines used are long-passaged and known to drift from primary tumour biology
Combination haematologic toxicity with a PARP inhibitor is entirely unknown
Whether the benefit requires an HR defect was not formally separated

intervention_label: MIF-CD74/CD44 axis blockade (4-IPP tool compound; ibudilast as a repurposing handle)
mechanism: Tumour-derived MIF signals through CD74 with CD44 as co-receptor, holding macrophages in an M2-like state and blunting CD8 T-cell function. 4-IPP covalently modifies the MIF tautomerase site and destabilises the protein; ibudilast, an old phosphodiesterase inhibitor, binds the same pocket allosterically.
rationale: The single-cell map of metastatic uLMS names MIF-CD74/CD44 as one of the dominant ligand-receptor circuits alongside exhausted CD8 T cells, M2 macrophages and N2 neutrophils, so this is a target read directly off the right disease and the right compartment. Her lesions were described radiologically as infiltrative and possibly inflammatory, which at minimum makes the myeloid compartment worth interrogating. In osteosarcoma, MIF blockade repolarised macrophages and improved anti-PD-1 activity, which is the closest functional test anyone has run in a sarcoma. Checkpoint blockade alone has failed repeatedly in LMS, so a mechanism aimed at why it fails is more interesting than another checkpoint agent.
novelty: No MIF-directed agent appears upstream in this case, and no MIF inhibitor is enrolling in any oncology trial; ibudilast's only cancer exposure was a completed glioblastoma combination study, none in sarcoma.

key_manuscripts.finding: Single-cell profiling of treatment-naive metastatic uterine LMS found exhausted CD8 T cells, M2-polarised macrophages and immature N2 neutrophils, with MIF-(CD74+CD44) signalling between T/B cells and CXCL8 driving angiogenesis and TAM polarisation.
Multiomics analysis nominated tumour-cell-derived MIF as a therapeutic target in osteosarcoma, where blocking it potentiated anti-PD-1 therapy.
4-IPP destabilised MIF and suppressed osteosarcoma tumourigenesis by reducing NF-kB/P-TEFb-mediated c-Myb transcription, giving the tool compound an in-vivo track record in a bone sarcoma.

developability: 4-IPP is a covalent tool compound with poor drug-like properties and no IND. Ibudilast is approved in Japan and has completed a glioblastoma trial, so it offers a faster path, but its MIF affinity is modest and nobody has tested it in sarcoma.
risks: MIF has physiological roles in innate immunity; sustained blockade carries unknown infection risk
The uLMS single-cell evidence is descriptive - one treatment-naive patient's metastases - with no perturbation experiment in this histology
4-IPP's tautomerase-site covalent chemistry may act off-target at the concentrations used
Ibudilast plasma exposure at approved dosing may not reach MIF-inhibitory levels
caveats: The uLMS evidence identifies the circuit but never tests blocking it; the therapeutic data all come from osteosarcoma and glioblastoma.

intervention_label: Aurora A kinase inhibition selected by the uLMS centrosome/spindle transcriptional program (MK-5108)
target_feature_label: High-grade uterine leiomyosarcoma histology; TP53-deficient mitotic background
mechanism: MK-5108 is a highly Aurora-A-selective ATP-competitive inhibitor. In uLMS, over half of the most overexpressed transcripts govern centrosome and spindle function - UBE2C, AURKA, AURKB, TPX2, PLK1 - so blocking Aurora A pushes cells with an already fragile mitotic apparatus into failed division and apoptosis.
rationale: Genome-wide profiling of myometrium, leiomyoma and leiomyosarcoma pointed at the mitotic apparatus as the single most consistently deranged program in uLMS, and Aurora A knockdown or inhibition killed metastasis-derived uLMS lines. The orthotopic experiment is the part I find persuasive: oral dosing shrank implants in a uterine model, not a flank tumour. A TP53-null background, which is expected in the large majority of uLMS and is what her plasma call would imply if tumour-derived, removes the G1 checkpoint that would otherwise let a cell survive a botched mitosis. The catch is that MK-5108 did not reliably synergise with gemcitabine or docetaxel, so it is a single-agent hypothesis, not a chemotherapy potentiator.
novelty: MK-5108 was abandoned after a single early-phase study and has no active development programme; no Aurora-directed agent appears in this case's trials, clinical-evidence or preclinical-evidence files.

key_manuscripts.finding: 26 of the 50 gene products most overexpressed in uLMS regulate mitotic centrosome and spindle function; Aurora A knockdown or MK-5108 induced apoptosis in LEIO285, LEIO505 and SK-LMS1. Oral MK-5108 at 30 or 60 mg/kg reduced implant number and size in an orthotopic uLMS model with raised intratumoral apoptosis.

developability: MK-5108 itself is effectively a tool compound now. Anyone pursuing this would either revive the chemotype or repeat the uLMS experiments with a current Aurora-A-selective molecule, which shifts the candidate towards trial_screener's territory the moment a clinical agent is substituted.
risks: Aurora A inhibitors carry class neutropenia and mucositis; alisertib's broad development largely disappointed
No synergy with gemcitabine or docetaxel was demonstrated, limiting combination strategies
The supporting work is from 2012 and has not been repeated in modern uLMS PDX models
Aurora A dependency was inferred from expression, not from a functional genomic screen in uLMS
caveats: Clinical-stage Aurora A inhibitors exist in other tumour types; what is novel here is the uLMS selection rationale, not the target class.

intervention_label: MYOCD / MRTF-SRF smooth-muscle lineage transcription-factor dependency
mechanism: Myocardin is the smooth-muscle-specific coactivator of serum response factor and sets the contractile differentiation program that defines this lineage. Removing it - genetically, or in principle by degrading it or blocking the MRTF/SRF interface with CCG-series compounds - collapses that program and, in the one cell line tested, proliferation with it.
rationale: Lineage-survival transcription factors have been the productive target class in several other histologies, and uLMS has an obvious candidate that nobody has drugged. MYOCD is amplified and overexpressed in most retroperitoneal LMS, and shRNA knockdown stripped smooth-muscle differentiation and slowed growth. Genomic subtyping later showed LMS splits along lineage lines that track survival, which strengthens the case that differentiation state is doing real work in this disease. I would call this the most under-explored idea on this list rather than the best-supported one: there is no MYOCD-directed molecule, and the MRTF/SRF tool compounds were built for fibrosis, not cancer.
novelty: No MYOCD or MRTF/SRF agent exists in oncology development, and nothing upstream in this case touches lineage transcription factors.

key_manuscripts.finding: MYOCD is amplified and overexpressed in most human retroperitoneal leiomyosarcomas, and shRNA knockdown in an amplified LMS line sharply reduced smooth-muscle differentiation and cell growth.

Genomic and transcriptomic analysis of 70 LMS genomes and 130 transcriptomes resolved three lineage-defined subtypes that arise very early and track with survival, supporting differentiation state as a structuring axis in this disease.

key_manuscripts.journal: Journal of Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics
key_manuscripts.finding: CCG-series small molecules block MRTF/SRF-regulated transcription and prevented fibrosis in vivo, establishing that the coactivator-SRF interface is chemically tractable outside oncology.

model_systems: retroperitoneal LMS tumours and one MYOCD-amplified LMS cell line
murine fibrosis models (for the MRTF/SRF chemotype)
developability: No clinical-grade molecule exists against MYOCD, and the CCG MRTF/SRF inhibitors are academic probes with fibrosis, not cancer, pharmacology behind them. A degrader or an interface inhibitor would have to be built from scratch, and the first question is whether uterine LMS carries the same MYOCD dependency the retroperitoneal tumours did.
risks: The functional work is in retroperitoneal LMS, not uterine; MYOCD amplification frequency in uLMS is lower
Smooth muscle is essential tissue - vascular, gastrointestinal, airway - so on-target toxicity could be severe
MRTF/SRF probes have modest potency and poorly characterised selectivity
Loss of differentiation could in principle select for a more aggressive dedifferentiated state
caveats: This is a target-validation proposal more than a drug proposal; the first experiment is whether uterine LMS models depend on MYOCD at all.

intervention_label: Glyoxalase-1 inhibition (BBGC) to potentiate trabectedin in soft-tissue sarcoma
target_feature_label: High-grade uterine leiomyosarcoma histology; planned trabectedin-containing first line
mechanism: BBGC is a cell-permeable diester prodrug that inhibits glyoxalase-1, the enzyme that detoxifies methylglyoxal. Letting methylglyoxal accumulate raises dicarbonyl stress and DNA/protein adduct burden, which appears to lower the threshold at which trabectedin's minor-groove adducts become lethal.
rationale: She is scheduled for doxorubicin plus trabectedin, so anything that raises trabectedin's ceiling in LMS is directly on-axis for how this disease will actually be treated. The screen that nominated BBGC used TCGA-SARC and sarcoma lines including leiomyosarcoma, and the combination held in vivo. Trabectedin's response rate as a single agent in LMS sits low enough that a sensitiser is a reasonable thing to want. I am holding this at emerging because the in-vivo work was done in a fibrosarcoma orthotopic model, not an LMS one.
novelty: BBGC is a laboratory glyoxalase-1 inhibitor with no IND and no registered trial; no glyoxalase or dicarbonyl-stress agent appears upstream in this case.

key_manuscripts.finding: An in-silico screen of GSEA M5190 and TCGA SARC nominated glyoxalase-1; BBGC enhanced trabectedin's antitumour effect across fibrosarcoma, leiomyosarcoma and liposarcoma cell lines and in a fibrosarcoma orthotopic model.

model_systems: fibrosarcoma, leiomyosarcoma, dedifferentiated and myxoid liposarcoma cell lines
developability: BBGC has no clinical-grade successor and its pharmacokinetics are unpublished. Any translation would need a drug-like GLO1 inhibitor plus a dedicated combination toxicology package with trabectedin, whose hepatic and myelosuppressive profile leaves little headroom.
risks: In-vivo confirmation is in fibrosarcoma, not leiomyosarcoma
Glyoxalase-1 is broadly expressed; systemic methylglyoxal accumulation has unclear organ consequences
Trabectedin hepatotoxicity and myelosuppression constrain how much a sensitiser can be added
Industry co-authorship on the source paper (PharmaMar) warrants the usual caution about combination framing

intervention_label: Copper loading to block ATP7B-mediated platinum efflux in uterine leiomyosarcoma
target_feature_label: High-grade uterine leiomyosarcoma histology; platinum resistance
mechanism: ATP7B is a copper-transporting P-type ATPase that also exports platinum drugs, and uLMS cells express it strongly. Preloading with copper sulfate occupies the transporter, platinum accumulates intracellularly instead of being pumped out, and cisplatin regains cytotoxicity.
rationale: Platinum is not part of standard uLMS therapy largely because the disease does not respond to it, and this work offers a concrete mechanistic reason rather than a shrug. Knocking down ATP7B dropped the cisplatin IC50 fourfold and turned a 5.8% xenograft response into 62.8%; copper pretreatment reproduced that pharmacologically. If it held up, it would reopen a whole drug class for a histology with few options. I rate the evidence emerging and not more: everything rests on SK-LMS-1 and its derivatives from a single group, and copper as a therapeutic is its own problem.
novelty: No copper- or ATP7B-directed strategy appears anywhere upstream in this case, and there is no registered trial of copper loading as a platinum sensitiser in sarcoma.

key_manuscripts.journal: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
key_manuscripts.finding: SK-LMS-1 uLMS cells expressed high ATP7B; suppressing it cut the cisplatin IC50 from 17.2 to 4.2 microM and raised xenograft response from 5.8% to 62.8%. Copper sulfate pretreatment at 15 microM for 3 hours reproduced the effect, raising intracellular platinum from 1.9 to 8.6 pg/cell.

developability: Systemic copper loading is not a therapeutic strategy anyone has developed; a selective ATP7B inhibitor would be the sensible molecule and none exists. Copper chelation, not copper loading, is where the clinical precedent sits, which makes this an inverted problem.
risks: Copper toxicity - hepatic and neurologic - is well documented and the therapeutic window is narrow
One cell line and its isogenic derivative from a single group; no PDX confirmation
Presupposes a platinum backbone that is not standard in uLMS
ATP7B expression in her tumour is unmeasured and would have to be shown first
caveats: Reopening platinum in uLMS is a large claim on thin data; treat the ATP7B expression finding as the durable part and the copper intervention as the weak part.

intervention_label: FANCM ablation in ALT-positive tumours (FANCM-RMI interaction inhibitors; FANCM antisense oligonucleotides)
target_feature_label: Alternative lengthening of telomeres (unmeasured; ~59% prevalence in LMS)
mechanism: ALT cells run continuous replication stress at telomeres and depend on FANCM's branchpoint translocase activity, working with the BTR complex, to keep that stress survivable. Removing FANCM - by disrupting the FANCM-RMI (MM2-BLM/RMI) interaction or by knocking the transcript down with antisense oligonucleotides - lets telomeric replication stress run away and kills ALT cells selectively.
rationale: ALT is the most prevalent and least exploited biological feature of leiomyosarcoma, and the dossier already records prevalence near 59% with ATRX loss as the recurrent driver. ATR inhibition, the obvious first move, failed replication in independent hands, so the field needs a different node - and FANCM has the cleanest genetic support. The antisense work got as far as an ALT-positive liposarcoma xenograft, which is at least a sarcoma even if it is the wrong one, and a second modality is in play through inhibitors of the FANCM-RMI interface. Nobody has tested any of it in a leiomyosarcoma model, and that is the experiment I would want run.
novelty: No FANCM-directed agent has an IND or a registered trial in any indication; this axis is absent from the case's trials, clinical-evidence and preclinical-evidence files, which cover ATR only.

key_manuscripts.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
key_manuscripts.finding: FANCM, BRCA1 and BLM cooperate to resolve replication stress at ALT telomeres, and losing FANCM drives lethal telomeric replication stress in ALT cells.
A fluorescence-polarisation assay was built specifically to screen for FANCM-RMI interaction inhibitors as ALT-directed agents, which means a tractable chemical-probe campaign is already underway.

CRISPR-Cas9 work validated FANCM as a dependency of ALT-positive cancers in vitro and in vivo, and a screened antisense gapmer (gapmer 14) knocked FANCM down, raised ALT activity to a toxic level and cut tumour growth in an ALT-positive liposarcoma xenograft.

developability: A screened antisense gapmer with in-vivo activity exists at academic scale, and the FANCM-RMI interface has a published screening assay, but neither has an IND-enabling package. Delivering an oligonucleotide to bilateral pulmonary metastases adds a formulation problem on top of the target problem.
risks: FANCM loss causes chromosome instability in normal cells and predisposes to Fanconi-like phenotypes
In-vivo proof of concept is in an ALT-positive liposarcoma, not leiomyosarcoma
Her ALT status is unmeasured - telomere FISH or a C-circle assay on tissue would have to come first
ATR inhibition's failure in ALT is a cautionary precedent for ALT-selectivity claims generally
caveats: ALT status is an assay she has not had; without it this is a population-level bet on a 59% prior, not a patient-level rationale.

intervention_label: SMARCAL1 annealing-helicase inhibition in ATRX-deficient, ALT-positive tumours
target_feature_label: ALT / ATRX loss (both unmeasured in this patient)
mechanism: SMARCAL1 is an annealing helicase that remodels stalled replication forks and localises to ALT-associated PML bodies. Depleting it in ALT-positive cells hyperactivates the ALT phenotype rather than shutting it down, producing G2 double-strand breaks and death by mitotic catastrophe.
rationale: This is the newest and most specific ALT dependency published, drawn from DepMap CRISPR data and then confirmed in patient-derived lines and intracranial xenografts with inducible knockdown extending survival. The selection marker - ATRX loss with ALT - is a recurrent combination in leiomyosarcoma, so the biological premise transfers even though the models do not. What I like about it is the mechanism: killing by pushing ALT harder is a different logic from starving it, and it might survive the ALT-selectivity problem that sank ATR inhibition. There is no inhibitor, which is the whole obstacle.
novelty: No SMARCAL1 inhibitor exists; the paper's own conclusion is that small-molecule development has yet to start. Nothing upstream in this case addresses fork-remodelling helicases.

key_manuscripts.finding: DepMap mining plus patient-derived models identified SMARCAL1 as selectively essential in ATRX-deficient ALT-positive glioma; depletion hyperactivated ALT, produced G2 double-strand breaks and mitotic catastrophe, and prolonged survival in intracranial xenografts.

developability: Genetic depletion only - no chemical matter of any kind. A leiomyosarcoma-relevant version would need the DepMap analysis re-run on sarcoma lines and then a full discovery campaign against an ATPase that has no precedent as a drug target.
risks: Every experiment is in glioma; no sarcoma model has been tested
Inducible RNAi is a kinder perturbation than a small molecule and often overstates a therapeutic window
SMARCAL1 loss in the germline causes Schimke immuno-osseous dysplasia, hinting at real on-target toxicity
Requires both ATRX status and ALT status, neither of which has been measured in this patient

intervention_label: Deregulating BLM at ALT telomeres via the SLX4IP/FANCM brake
mechanism: BLM helicase drives telomere recombination in ALT but has to be restrained, and SLX4IP acts in parallel to FANCM as that brake. Releasing the brake - or conversely blocking BLM outright with a probe such as ML216 - pushes ALT telomeres past the recombination load they can tolerate.
rationale: Both directions on this axis are lethal to ALT cells in principle, which is unusual and worth testing empirically rather than arguing about. It sits alongside the FANCM idea as a second node on the same pathway, so a lab pursuing FANCM should test this in the same experiment rather than as a separate programme. I am marking it speculative deliberately: one Molecular Cell paper and a 2025 preprint, no in-vivo work, no leiomyosarcoma model, and BLM chemical probes with poor selectivity.
novelty: Neither SLX4IP nor BLM has any clinical-grade molecule or registered trial; the axis is absent from all upstream files in this case.

key_manuscripts.finding: SLX4IP antagonises promiscuous BLM activity during ALT maintenance, establishing that ALT telomeres need active restraint of recombination rather than only its promotion.
SLX4IP acts in parallel to FANCM to limit BLM-dependent replication stress at ALT telomeres, so losing both brakes is more toxic than losing either alone.

developability: Nothing beyond research reagents. BLM probes such as ML216 exist but are weak and promiscuous, and SLX4IP is a scaffold protein with no obvious binding pocket.
risks: BLM loss causes Bloom syndrome with cancer predisposition, so systemic inhibition is a hard sell
One peer-reviewed paper plus an unrefereed preprint
No in-vivo data at all, in any tumour type
Depends on ALT status that has not been measured here
caveats: Best treated as a mechanistic extension of the FANCM candidate rather than a standalone programme.

intervention_label: CIP2A-TOPBP1 interface disruption in HR-deficient leiomyosarcoma
target_feature_label: Homologous-recombination deficiency (unmeasured; ~35% of LMS carry HRD signatures)
mechanism: CIP2A and TOPBP1 tether shattered chromosome fragments together through mitosis and support mitotic DNA synthesis and microhomology-mediated end joining. HR-deficient cells lean on that tethering to survive their own break burden, so breaking the CIP2A-TOPBP1 interface kills them while sparing HR-proficient cells.
rationale: Roughly a third of leiomyosarcomas carry HRD signatures, and the dossier's strongest lineage-matched signal is already the DNA-repair axis. CIP2A-TOPBP1 is a genuinely undrugged node in that axis, which puts it in a different category from PARP, POLQ and USP1 - all of which now have clinical molecules and belong to the trial screener. The mechanism is also mitotic rather than replicative, so it should not share cross-resistance with PARP inhibition, which matters if she is eventually given one. It is a protein-protein interface with no chemical matter, so this is a target proposal.
novelty: No CIP2A or TOPBP1 agent exists in development and none is registered in any trial; the axis appears nowhere upstream in this case.

key_manuscripts.finding: The CIP2A-TOPBP1 complex tethers chromosome fragments through mitosis and is synthetic lethal with BRCA mutation, with loss selectively killing HR-deficient cells.
The same axis facilitates mitotic DNA synthesis and microhomology-mediated end joining, extending the dependency beyond simple fragment tethering and widening the potential selection biomarker.

model_systems: BRCA1/2-mutant and isogenic HR-deficient cell lines
developability: A protein-protein interaction with no reported small-molecule or degrader chemistry. Even an early campaign is years from a testable molecule, and a leiomyosarcoma-specific validation experiment does not yet exist.
risks: All evidence is from breast/ovarian BRCA-mutant contexts, none in sarcoma
Requires HR deficiency, which is unmeasured here and would need tissue HRD testing
Interface inhibitors of this class have a poor historical hit rate
CIP2A also acts as a PP2A inhibitor, so on-target effects may be pleiotropic

intervention_label: ADAR1 inhibition in BRCA1/2-mutant or HR-deficient tumours
mechanism: ADAR1 edits double-stranded RNA so cytosolic sensors do not read it as viral. In BRCA1/2-mutant cells the baseline interferon tone is already elevated, and removing ADAR1 tips that into autocrine interferon poisoning - a self-inflicted, cell-intrinsic interferon response that is lethal.
rationale: Two of this case's problems point the same way: an unmeasured HRD fraction that is substantial in LMS, and a microenvironment that single-cell work describes as exhausted and myeloid-dominated. An ADAR1 dependency would hit the tumour cell directly and, as a side effect, raise the interferon signal that a T-cell-excluded tumour is short of. Whether that second effect helps or simply drives PD-L1 up is unresolved and would be the first thing I would ask a lab to test. Nothing about this has been examined in sarcoma.
novelty: ADAR1 inhibitors are at chemical-probe stage with no registered oncology trial; ADAR1 appears nowhere in this case's upstream files.

key_manuscripts.finding: ADAR1 loss is synthetic lethal in BRCA1/2-mutant cancers, acting through autocrine interferon poisoning downstream of cytosolic RNA sensing rather than through a DNA-repair mechanism.

developability: ADAR1 deaminase-domain inhibitors and degraders are early discovery-stage across several groups, with nothing in IND-enabling work publicly. Any sarcoma application would first need the dependency shown in HR-deficient LMS models, which do not currently exist in usable form.
risks: ADAR1 loss in normal tissue drives interferonopathy; systemic inhibition may be poorly tolerated
Dependency was defined in BRCA-mutant breast/ovarian contexts, not sarcoma
Interferon induction may raise PD-L1 and other adaptive resistance signals
Her HR status is unmeasured, so even the selection biomarker is hypothetical

intervention_label: Hypomethylating plus HDAC-inhibitor priming to induce MAGE-A4 / NY-ESO-1 / PRAME before HLA-A*02:01-restricted T-cell redirection
target_feature_label: HLA-A*02:01 confirmed; cancer/testis antigen expression untested
mechanism: CT antigen promoters are silenced by CpG methylation, and decitabine demethylation restores transcription while HDAC inhibition opens the corresponding chromatin. The same treatment raises MHC class I and ICAM-1, so a tumour that was invisible to an HLA-A*02:01-restricted TCR or ImmTAC becomes both antigen-positive and better able to present it.
rationale: Her HLA-A*02:01 is confirmed, which is the harder half of the eligibility question, and the missing half - MAGE-A4, NY-ESO-1 or PRAME expression - is exactly the variable this strategy manipulates. If the antigen IHC comes back negative, every A*02:01-restricted programme closes; a priming strategy is the only published route that reopens it. Decitabine already does this in sarcoma cell lines, a demethylating pretreatment elicited CT-antigen-specific CD8 responses in osteosarcoma, and a 2026 preprint extends sequential decitabine-then-entinostat to poorly immunogenic sarcoma in vivo. Both priming drugs are old and cheap, so the obstacle is the schedule and the pairing, not the molecules.
novelty: No trial anywhere pairs epigenetic antigen induction with an HLA-A*02:01-restricted TCR-T or ImmTAC product in sarcoma; the case's upstream files carry the TCR-T products but nothing that manufactures the antigen.

key_manuscripts.finding: Decitabine upregulated cancer/testis antigens, MHC molecules and ICAM-1 on sarcoma cells and improved immune recognition, which is the antigen-plus-presentation combination an HLA-restricted product needs.
Demethylating pretreatment induced a CT-antigen-specific CD8 T-cell response against osteosarcoma, taking the idea past expression and into functional recognition.

Sequential decitabine then entinostat raised silenced-gene expression including cancer/testis antigens and MHC class I in a Kras-driven murine sarcoma, more than either agent alone, and vaccination with the treated cells was immunogenic.

developability: Decitabine and entinostat are both available, so what is missing is a sequencing study: how much antigen induction is enough, whether it persists long enough to overlap a cell-therapy infusion, and whether it holds in leiomyosarcoma rather than in the osteosarcoma and murine models where it was shown.
risks: Antigen induction is heterogeneous and may not reach the threshold a TCR product's screening assay demands
Hypomethylating agents also raise antigen on normal tissue, which could worsen on-target off-tumour toxicity from an affinity-enhanced TCR
Myelosuppression from priming compounds lymphodepletion before cell therapy
No leiomyosarcoma model has been used for any of this
caveats: Induced antigen is not the same as constitutive antigen, and no TCR-T programme currently accepts induced expression for eligibility.

intervention_label: SMARCB1 G344Afs*13 neo-open-reading-frame peptide as a personalised HLA-A*02:01 immunogen
mechanism: A frameshift generates a short stretch of amino acids found nowhere in the normal proteome before the premature stop, and those residues can yield peptides with no thymic tolerance. If any of them binds HLA-A*02:01, it becomes a target for a vaccine, a TCR, or a peptide-HLA-directed antibody.
rationale: Her two confirmed pieces of information point at each other: an A*02:01 allele and a frameshift variant. Frameshift-derived neo-ORFs are the most immunogenic class of neoantigen precisely because they are wholly foreign, and unlike the cancer/testis antigens this would not require inducing anything. That said, G344Afs*13 gives only about thirteen novel residues before the stop, so the peptide space is small and there may simply be no A*02:01 binder in it - a question answered in an afternoon with a binding predictor and a stabilisation assay. Everything downstream is also contingent on the variant being tumour-derived and expressed, which plasma sequencing alone does not establish.
novelty: Entirely case-specific; no product, no programme, and no publication addresses this variant. Nothing upstream in the case touches neoantigen-directed approaches.
model_systems: none - in-silico binding prediction and peptide-MHC stabilisation would be the first step
developability: Nothing exists. The sequence of work is: confirm the variant on tissue and show the transcript escapes nonsense-mediated decay, predict and then measure A*02:01 binding for the thirteen novel residues, and only then consider a TCR or peptide-HLA antibody. Any one of those steps can end it.
risks: Nonsense-mediated decay may destroy the transcript before any peptide is made
Thirteen novel residues is a small peptide space; an A*02:01 binder may not exist
The variant is plasma-only and unconfirmed on tissue, and SMARCB1 alteration is rare in uterine smooth-muscle tumours
A heterozygous frameshift means wild-type protein is still present, so this is an immunological target rather than a dependency
caveats: Listed because the two confirmed facts in her profile intersect here, not because there is evidence behind it. No key manuscripts exist for this specific idea.

intervention_label: DNA-PK inhibition (peposertib) with unconventionally low-dose doxorubicin in leiomyosarcoma
mechanism: LMS lines screened by genome-wide shRNA come out dependent on PRKDC and RPA2, consistent with hyper-reliance on non-homologous end joining to survive their own copy-number chaos. Blocking DNA-PK while giving doxorubicin at a low sensitising dose converts anthracycline damage into unrepaired breaks.
rationale: The best lineage-matched DNA-repair idea I found: 287 sequenced LMS, HRD signatures in 35%, and peposertib plus low-dose doxorubicin controlled 5 of 7 LMS mouse models without toxicity. It also lines up with her planned doxorubicin-containing first line.
exclusion_reason: Already clinical-stage and therefore trial_screener's territory: NCT05711615 is recruiting peposertib with low-dose liposomal doxorubicin in advanced sarcoma with metastatic and unresectable leiomyosarcoma named among the eligible histologies. Flagged here because it did not appear in this case's trials.jsonl and is worth a second look on the clinical track.

intervention_label: ATR inhibition selected by ALT status (elimusertib, camonsertib)
mechanism: ATR coordinates the homologous recombination that ALT telomeres depend on, so inhibiting it was expected to be selectively toxic to ALT-positive cells.
rationale: Elimusertib showed in-vivo activity in ATRX-mutant uLMS models, and ALT runs near 59% in LMS.
exclusion_reason: Covered upstream: the researcher's preclinical_evidence file already carries both the original ALT-ATR claim and the failed replication showing ALT cells are not generally ATR-hypersensitive. ATR inhibitors are also enrolling broadly, which puts the agents on the clinical track.

intervention_label: WEE1 inhibition selected by ATRX loss or TP53 deficiency (adavosertib, azenosertib)
mechanism: WEE1 restrains CDK1 at the G2/M boundary; removing it in cells that have already lost the p53-dependent G1 checkpoint forces premature mitosis with unrepaired DNA.
rationale: A genome-wide CRISPR screen found ATRX-mutant cancers selectively vulnerable to WEE1 inhibition, and ATRX loss is recurrent in uLMS.
exclusion_reason: The WEE1 inhibitor class is clinical-stage across multiple sponsors and indications, so it belongs to trial_screener rather than to a horizon scan.

intervention_label: PKMYT1 inhibition (lunresertib / RP-6306) in a TP53-deficient background
mechanism: PKMYT1 phosphorylates CDK1 in parallel with WEE1; inhibiting it drives unscheduled mitotic entry in cells with high replication stress and no functional p53.
rationale: TP53 loss is expected in most uLMS, and lunresertib has been paired with platinum specifically in TP53-altered uterine cancers.
exclusion_reason: Already enrolling: lunresertib is in multiple phase 1 studies including NCT06107868 in TP53-altered ovarian and uterine cancer. Clinical-stage, so trial_screener's job.

intervention_label: Polymerase theta (POLQ) inhibition in HR-deficient tumours
mechanism: POLQ drives microhomology-mediated end joining, the backup pathway HR-deficient cells depend on; blocking it is synthetic lethal with HR loss and resensitises PARP-inhibitor-resistant tumours.
rationale: Roughly a third of LMS carry HRD signatures, which would be the selection marker.
exclusion_reason: ART4215 completed a phase 1 in advanced solid tumours (NCT04991480) and other POLQ programmes have followed, so the class sits with trial_screener.

intervention_label: USP1 inhibition in HR-deficient tumours
mechanism: USP1 deubiquitinates PCNA and FANCD2, and its loss is synthetic lethal in BRCA-mutant backgrounds, including after PARP-inhibitor resistance.
rationale: Same HRD selection logic as the POLQ candidate, with a non-overlapping node.
exclusion_reason: Clinical-stage: TNG348 ran a phase 1 with a PARP inhibitor in BRCA-mutant/HRD-positive solid tumours (NCT06065059) and further USP1 programmes have entered trials. Trial_screener's territory.

intervention_label: KIF18A inhibition in chromosomally unstable, aneuploid tumours
mechanism: KIF18A is dispensable in near-diploid cells but required for viable mitosis in cells with high chromosomal instability, giving a wide therapeutic index in aneuploid tumours.
rationale: LMS carries a median fraction-of-genome-altered above 0.6, which is exactly the CIN phenotype this class exploits.
exclusion_reason: The class went clinical while this idea was maturing: sovilnesib, VLS-1488, ATX-295 and several others are recruiting in solid tumours. Belongs to trial_screener.

intervention_label: LP-184, an acylfulvene alkylating agent for HR-deficient tumours
mechanism: LP-184 is bioactivated by PTGR1 and produces DNA adducts that HR-deficient cells cannot resolve.
rationale: Reported activity across HRD solid tumours would map onto the HRD fraction of LMS.
exclusion_reason: In clinical development (NCT05933265, active), so it sits with trial_screener rather than here.

intervention_label: TREM2 blockade to remodel the suppressive myeloid compartment
mechanism: TREM2 marks immunosuppressive tumour-associated macrophages; blocking it shifts the myeloid compartment and improves checkpoint-blockade responses in mouse tumours.
rationale: The metastatic uLMS microenvironment is dominated by M2-like macrophages, which is the compartment TREM2 antibodies target.
exclusion_reason: PY314 took anti-TREM2 into a phase 1 in advanced solid tumours (NCT04691375, terminated), so the approach has already been through clinical development and is not an early-horizon idea.

intervention_label: CXCL8/CXCR2 axis blockade against tumour-promoting neutrophils
mechanism: CXCL8 signalling through CXCR1/2 recruits and polarises the immature N2 neutrophils that populate uLMS metastases and supports angiogenesis.
rationale: The uLMS single-cell map names CXCL8 as a dominant axis alongside MIF, so the target is lineage-matched.
exclusion_reason: CXCR2 antagonists including navarixin and reparixin have run oncology trials in several tumour types, which places the class with trial_screener.

intervention_label: EZH2 or PRC2 degradation as a next-generation SMARCB1-deficiency strategy
mechanism: Because the EZH2 dependency in SWI/SNF-mutant cells is substantially non-catalytic, degrading EZH2 or destabilising PRC2 should do what enzymatic inhibition cannot.
rationale: This would be the obvious next chemistry step if the SMARCB1 branch were live.
exclusion_reason: The premise fails before the chemistry matters. Her variant is a single heterozygous frameshift called on plasma only, while the entire dependency rests on biallelic INI1 protein loss, and 170 consecutive uterine smooth-muscle tumours all retained SMARCB1 (PMID 34271067). No smooth-muscle model of this dependency exists, and both BRD9 degrader programmes were discontinued.

intervention_label: Peptide-HLA-A*02:01 bispecific antibody against a TP53 mutation-derived neoantigen
mechanism: A single-chain diabody binds the mutant p53 peptide presented on HLA-A*02:01 and recruits T cells through CD3, turning an intracellular driver mutation into a surface target.
rationale: Her HLA-A*02:01 is confirmed, which is the restriction element this class requires.
exclusion_reason: Mechanism does not fit the variant. The published reagents target the R175H missense neoepitope; TP53 Q52* is a nonsense variant that produces no analogous mutant peptide, and it carries an unresolved clonal-haematopoiesis caveat on top of that.
